clue.text: Board members aim to sermonise

parts.note: to aim something is to direct it at a target
to sermonise is to orate, deliver a speech

explanation.surface: Members of a board set out to lecture everyone, like pompous executives.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of directors collectively forms a board, so the word names the members as a group.

clue.text: Energy spent, breaks down in soul venue

indicators.note: something spent is used up and gone, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: a car engine that breaks down dies
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soul music club loses power and the equipment fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soul venue' suggests a music club; it is the classical underworld where the souls of the dead go.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the underworld gives his name to the realm of the dead, home of departed spirits.

clue.text: Parry, holding short sword in both hands

indicators.note: the hands hold the sword between them

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left hands

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing its last letter

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A fencer parries while gripping a short sword two-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry a blow is to ward it off or drive it back, which is to fend it away.

clue.text: Firm in time makes money

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A company eventually becomes profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in circulation as currency make up a nation's metal cash, so it is money.

clue.text: Alien asleep on spacecraft

parts.note: someone out cold or out for the count is asleep
a lander is a craft that touches down on another world

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial dozes aboard a spaceship.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner or stranger from far away is an outsider, so the word means an alien.

clue.text: Area near steamer that's extremely deep

parts.note: by means near, beside
SS, steamship, is the prefix for a steamer

explanation.surface: Waters near a steamship that are very deep indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless chasm or gulf is a place of enormous depth, something extremely deep.

clue.text: Ancient ascetic catching cold shows perfect form

indicators.note: the ascetic catches, takes inside, the cold

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An old hermit catches a cold yet looks the picture of health.
explanation.definitionFit: The quintessence of something is its purest, most perfect embodiment, its ideal form.

clue.text: Dry run cancelled to provide encouragement

indicators.note: something cancelled is struck out, so the run's letter is removed from the dry word

parts.note: dry land is arid
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rehearsal is called off, as a way of offering support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry run' looks like one phrase for a rehearsal, but 'Dry' and 'run' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To help or assist someone is to back them up, giving them support and encouragement.

clue.text: Angelica's reformulated as medicament

indicators.note: a recipe reformulated has its ingredients reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The herb angelica is reworked into a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Angelica is a medicinal herb, so the surface plausibly describes a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller such as aspirin is a drug, a type of medicine.

clue.text: Nonsense that follows from bigamy in Bow?

definitions.text: that follows from bigamy in Bow?
definitions.meaning: in Cockney, 'my old Dutch' is a wife, so a bigamist in the East End has two of them

explanation.surface: Gibberish results from a man marrying twice in an East End district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockneys, for whom 'Dutch' (from duchess) means wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that cannot be understood is gibberish, so the phrase means meaningless talk.

clue.text: Speciousness ruined story about wrecked ship

indicators.note: the reworked story goes around, about, the other reworked word
a ruined story is one broken up, so its letters are rearranged
a wrecked ship is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misleading tale is ruined by its account of a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: The shipwreck story hides two separate anagrams, signalled by 'ruined' and 'wrecked', with 'about' wrapping one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious reasoning is plausible but false, which is exactly what clever misleading argument amounts to.

clue.text: United supporters returned in usual chaos

indicators.note: something returned comes back the other way, so the supporters are read backwards

parts.note: football supporters are fans
U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: Manchester United fans come back home to the usual mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is military slang: 'situation normal, all fouled up', which makes 'usual chaos' a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang acronym for a normal state of muddle, so routine disorder is what it means.

clue.text: Mistress last month put in clinic close to Chelsea

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the clinic word

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a health clinic
ULT, short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A kept woman was admitted last month to a clinic near Chelsea, the smart London district.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's wife or concubine bears this title, so a royal mistress in a harem fits.

clue.text: Surveillance requires excellent image

parts.note: super means excellent
a vision is an image seen in the mind

explanation.surface: Good monitoring needs a sharp camera picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseeing and watching over others is keeping them under observation, which is surveillance.

clue.text: What makes Angelenos who they are, backing country?

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the phrase is read from the end

parts.words: What makes Angelenos who they are
parts.note: Angelenos are people of Los Angeles, LA, and their genes make them who they are: LA GENES

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the identity of Los Angeles residents, asked of some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Angelenos are residents of Los Angeles; their LA genes, written backwards, give the West African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation in West Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Minister in service flat emptied receptacle

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A clergyman in a service flat empties a bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service flat' looks like one phrase, but 'in service' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain to the armed forces is a clergyman serving the military, so a minister in the services.

clue.text: Controls in place here to run committee

parts.note: to dash is to run quickly
a board is a committee of directors

explanation.surface: The chairman sets up a takeover of a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car the instrument panel holds the switches and gauges, so the controls are found here.

clue.text: Enduring blues act, crowd confined

indicators.note: the crowd is held inside, confined by, the act

parts.note: an act is a deed
a press is a dense crowd of people

explanation.surface: A blues band is playing, and the crowd is penned in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering low spirits is feeling down, so having the blues means being glum and miserable.

clue.text: Medic in film about strangely shy Scotsman

indicators.note: the film goes about, around, the reworked word

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a film

indicators.note: strangely signals the letters of shy are jumbled

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A doctor stars in a film about a peculiarly bashful Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means around, not 'concerning': the film word wraps the jumbled shyness, with 'strangely' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified doctor of medicine is a medic, the same professional.

clue.text: One may have blown it in expressing disapproval

definitions.text: One may have blown it in expressing disapproval

parts.words: One may have blown it in expressing disapproval
parts.note: a rude noise made with tongue and lips, a Bronx cheer, is blown at someone to show contempt; the fruit sense is a decoy

explanation.surface: Someone who messed up while voicing disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown it' suggests failing, but here you literally blow the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude noise made by blowing through the lips shows derision, named after a fruit in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Advantage to accept free bit

indicators.note: the advantage takes in, accepts, the other word

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or advantage
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A benefit is offered for taking a little something for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like a small piece; it is the horse's mouthpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A light snaffle used with a curb on a horse's bridle is a kind of bit.

clue.text: Article in pipeline bringing money to Shylock

indicators.note: the article is placed in the pipeline

parts.note: a duct is a channel or pipe
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item in the pipeline brings cash to the moneylender of The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice reckons in this gold coin of Venice, so it is his currency.

clue.text: Flies in sink water mixed with leaves

parts.note: to dip is to sink briefly

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred up
the with letter leaves, departing from the reworked water

explanation.surface: Insects drop into a basin of water stirred with foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage, but it means W departs: WATER less W is reworked into TERA.
explanation.definitionFit: True flies form an order of two-winged insects, given its scientific name in zoology.

clue.text: Single knight having impressive physique that's essential

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
N is the chess notation for a knight
someone well muscled is described as built

explanation.surface: A lone knight with a powerful frame proves indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built in is an inherent, intrinsic part of a thing, so it is essential to it.

clue.text: Cast shortened the series

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, losing a letter from the middle

parts.note: a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: The cast of a TV series is reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a ball is to fling or hurl it, so it means the same as toss.

clue.text: Challenge validity of attractive person's claim?

definitions.meaning: to call into question the reliability of a witness or statement
a lovely person might say 'I'm a peach'

explanation.surface: Disputing whether a good-looking person's assertion is true.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as three words, 'I'm a peach', a peach being an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit testimony by questioning its truthfulness is the legal sense, alongside charging an official.

clue.text: Stadium in region accommodating any number

indicators.note: the region accommodates, takes in, the number

parts.note: an area is a region
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A sports ground in the district can seat any number of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed space for sports or performance is a venue like a stadium.

clue.text: If only I'd backed Union member

indicators.note: going backwards, so the phrase is reversed

parts.note: a wistful 'O had I' means if only I had

explanation.surface: A regretful trade unionist wishes they had supported something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' here is the United States, so a member is one of the states.
explanation.definitionFit: A state in the American federation is a member of the Union, in the US sense.

clue.text: Gather the ambassador will be furious

parts.note: to gather funds is to raise them
HE, His Excellency, is how an ambassador is addressed
'LL is the contraction of will

explanation.surface: Collect yourself: the ambassador is going to be livid.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a huge angry fuss and protest loudly is to rage, so being furious fits.

clue.text: Welshman raised in Penylan

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the letters are reversed
the letters are found within the place name

explanation.surface: A Welsh man was brought up in Penylan, a district of Cardiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh male first name, as borne by Olympic long-jumper Lyn Davies, so a Welsh man.

clue.text: Rebuffed university sort's acknowledgment

indicators.note: something rebuffed is pushed back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a don is a university teacher; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A snubbed academic gets a mere recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is a silent gesture of greeting or agreement, so a sign of recognition.

clue.text: Donna playing around with stove lit sometimes

indicators.note: the reworked name goes around the next letter
playing with the name means its letters are moved about

parts.note: an Aga is a big cooking range, a British brand of stove
a fire that is lit is said to be in

explanation.surface: Donna occasionally fiddles about with a lit stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges DONNA into NOAND, and 'around' puts W inside it. An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range found in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally, from time to time, at irregular intervals: all synonyms of the phrase.
